paper-batcher-learning-construct-cost-20.summary: This paper presents Batcher, a system for big data processing platforms that learns to group excessive small queries into cost-efficient batches using a query-batch cost estimation model and multi-staged cluster refinement, achieving up to 5.4x performance improvement over prior small-query handling techniques. To scale two real-world datasets (BRA and eBay) up to 1TB for scalability experiments, the authors used SDV's Gaussian copula-based model to learn the data distribution and generate synthetic datasets of desired size while preserving statistical characteristics. SDV is run as an off-the-shelf data-generation tool to support the paper's scalability evaluation, not as a subject of study.

It finds that simpler techniques like SMOTE-Tomek and Bootstrap better approximate real data distributions than deep generative approaches. CTGAN, TVAE, and GaussianCopula are run as three of the eight synthetic data generation techniques evaluated, benchmarked against SMOTE variants and Bootstrap sampling for downstream classifier performance.

To augment the sparse proximity-based vehicle data, the authors train a Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN) with 200 epochs, configuring discrete and continuous columns, generating 5,400 synthetic vehicle trajectory records that are merged with real data and validated via statistical distribution comparisons. CTGAN is run directly as the generator producing the synthetic data augmentation that feeds the downstream peer-report and reputation pipeline.

The best-performing pipeline combined a stacked ensemble with 'GAN imputation' and random under/oversampling across all four datasets. The reference list cites the CTGAN paper, but no passage in the extracted full text engages with SDV's CTGAN directly, leaving it unclear whether the GAN-based imputation method used is SDV's CTGAN or a separately cited GAN architecture.

paper-graph-trust-assessment-secure-2026.summary: This paper proposes a graph-based trust assessment framework for pre-deployment security analysis of software artifacts in service-oriented 6G architectures, using Node2Vec embeddings from a sample-similarity graph to derive trust-aware indicators for a JavaScript malicious-artifact detection dataset, feeding classifiers whose outputs become trust scores for orchestration and zero-trust policy decisions. CTGAN is applied during training exclusively to oversample the minority (malicious) class to mitigate class imbalance, trained only within each cross-validation fold to avoid leakage, and compared favorably against traditional oversampling like SMOTE. CTGAN is run as the class-imbalance data-augmentation step within the broader trust-assessment pipeline.

The work cites the CTGAN paper in connection with this generative data-augmentation approach, though the full text needed to confirm exactly how CTGAN was used was not available.

CTGAN and TVAE are set against SMOTE and TabDDPM, placing SDV's synthesizers between a classical oversampler and a diffusion model on the same task.

paper-toothed-nozzle-optimization-enhanc.summary: This paper develops a hybrid CTGAN-XGBoost model to predict interlayer tensile strength and area proportion coefficient in 3D-printed concrete made with toothed nozzles, using explanatory analysis to identify key nozzle design parameters and validating optimized designs experimentally. CTGAN is used to augment the limited experimental dataset before XGBoost performs the strength prediction. SDV's CTGAN is run as the generator producing synthetic training data that feeds the whole predictive pipeline.

paper-use-what-scenarios-help-2026.summary: This paper introduces AIMEN, a deep-learning framework that predicts adverse labor outcomes (e.g., cerebral palsy risk) from maternal, fetal, obstetrical, and intrapartum factors and generates counterfactual explanations for its predictions. To address severe class imbalance and a small dataset (1457 cases, 112 abnormal), AIMEN's default data-generation module uses CTGAN for synthetic oversampling, with variants exploring relaxed feature bounds and silhouette-score filtering, and is compared against an ADASYN-based variant. CTGAN, cited as reference [62], is run directly as the generator underlying the whole empirical pipeline, with distributional similarity (Wasserstein distance, MMD) and downstream classification performance used to validate its synthetic output against ADASYN.

paper-visibility-nowcasting-south-korea-.summary: This study proposes a machine learning and deep learning framework to nowcast atmospheric visibility in six major South Korean cities, addressing severe class imbalance in low-visibility events and a distributional shift between training and test periods. The authors compare SMOTENC, CTGAN, and a hierarchical SMOTENC+CTGAN augmentation strategy across multiple minority-class oversampling scenarios (7,000/10,000/20,000 synthetic points), evaluating fidelity via Wasserstein distance and UMAP/KDE visualizations before feeding augmented data into an ensemble of five classifiers. CTGAN, run with its own hyperparameter optimization, is used as one of the core data augmentation generators for the minority visibility classes, compared and combined with SMOTENC.

paper-istructtab-structured-feature-sequ.summary: This paper proposes iStructTab, a multimodal learning framework that formulates image-tabular feature fusion as a Column Permutation Problem, using a graph-enhanced descriptor sequencing algorithm (GEDS) combined with an order-aware efficient transformer to reduce feature dispersion and improve predictive performance across six image-tabular benchmarks. As a data preprocessing step for one of these datasets (DVM, a car image-attribute dataset), missing tabular values are imputed using CTGAN. CTGAN is run as an imputation tool on a single dataset among several, not as part of the paper's core methodological contribution.

paper-rct-synthetic-tabular-framework-20.summary: Compares two ways of generating synthetic randomized controlled trial data: a simultaneous framework in which a single model produces the whole table, and a sequential framework in which baseline covariates are generated first, treatment is then allocated at random to mimic the trial design, and post-allocation variables including the outcome follow from regression execution models fitted one variable at a time. Three generators are carried through both frameworks, CTGAN, adversarial random forests and an R-vine copula, and the authors conclude that the sequential R-vine copula route best reproduces the features of the real trial data. CTGAN is trained and sampled as one of the compared generation algorithms in both frameworks, and the paper sets out its mode-specific normalization and its conditional generator with training-by-sampling, so an SDV generator is run as a full arm of the study's empirical program.

paper-deep-synthesis-insider-intrusion-2.summary: This paper proposes DS-IID, a deep-learning insider-threat detection model that uses deep feature synthesis to build user profiles from event logs and a binary classifier to flag malicious insiders, while also testing whether it can distinguish real from AI-generated synthetic user profiles. To create the synthetic profiles used for this second task, the authors employ SDV's ready-made Gaussian Copula, CTGAN, TVAE, and CopulaGAN synthesizers trained on a schema of real CERT user-profile data, and they evaluate the synthesizers with SDV/SDMetrics quality-report scores (Data Validity, Data Structure, Column Shapes, Column Pair Trends). SDV is run directly as the generator suite producing the synthetic threat/user-profile data that the whole second half of the empirical evaluation is built on.

paper-ai4sweng-manifest-empowering-futur.summary: This is a project manifest paper introducing AI4SWEng, a Horizon Europe-funded consortium project (2025-2028) that aims to build an AI-powered software engineering suite spanning code generation, debugging, security, and project management, with emphasis on trustworthy AI and large language models. The paper is a strategic/positioning document describing the project's goals and consortium rather than an empirical study. It lists a reference to the original SDV (Synthetic Data Vault) DSAA 2016 paper, apparently as part of a broader citation list, with no visible discussion of running or engaging with the tool in the abstract.

It compares sampling-based, Bayesian-network, hybrid/transformer, and diffusion approaches, discussing trade-offs in accuracy, privacy, and resource cost. Three augmentation techniques are tested -- SMOTENC, Gaussian Copula, and CTGAN -- with CTGAN trained per fold (100 epochs, batch size 128) and results showing modest, model-dependent gains. CTGAN, the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN, is run as one of several data-augmentation methods evaluated against SMOTENC and Gaussian Copula.

paper-mixgan-hybrid-semi-supervised-2025.summary: This paper proposes MixGAN, a DDoS detection framework for cloud-integrated IoT networks that combines a 1-D WideResNet backbone, a CTGAN-based conditional sample generator, and a MixUp-Average-Sharpen semi-supervised strategy to address severe class imbalance and label scarcity. Experiments on NSL-KDD, BoT-IoT, and CICIoT2023 show accuracy and TPR/TNR gains over SMOTE and other baselines. The authors build their own CTGAN implementation, explicitly following the architecture of the original CTGAN paper (three-layer MLPs, Wasserstein loss with gradient penalty) rather than running the SDV-dev package, to generate class-conditional synthetic minority-class traffic for both offline augmentation and online pseudo-label refinement.

In its related-work discussion of synthetic tabular data quality assessment, it cites the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) as an example of a framework that assesses generated-data quality by comparing distributions of real and synthetic samples, contrasting this with its own cross-table detection approach. SDV is only cited as prior work characterizing distribution-comparison quality frameworks, not run in the paper's experiments.

The generative route, KT-GAN, runs the ctgan package at version 0.7.3 with default parameters as the data generator, so one of the paper's two competing methods is CTGAN used unmodified inside a knowledge-transfer pipeline.

CTGAN and TVAE are run as two of several synthesizers under evaluation, with CTGAN cited to the original NeurIPS paper.

CTGAN and TVAE, both attributed to the SDV library, are run as baseline generators that are shown to disregard temporal dependencies between flows.

The best-performing model overall used the Gaussian Copula synthesis technique combined with CatBoost, achieving the highest F1 score and AUC among all tested combinations. SDV's CTGAN, TVAE, CopulaGAN, and Gaussian Copula synthesizers are run as data-augmentation generators, one of which (Gaussian Copula) produces the paper's headline best result.

paper-split-discard-pretraining-2023.summary: Pre-trains a generator on a split of the data and discards part of it to limit what the released model can memorise, aiming for utility without the privacy cost. The comparison is against CTAB-GAN+ and its variants, which descend from CTGAN rather than being it.

paper-generation-alleviate-privacy-conce.summary: This paper proposes a synthetic tabular data generation methodology for an Intrusion Detection System (IDS) dataset, combining feature selection with GAN-based generators to address privacy concerns and class imbalance in cybersecurity data. It trains two GAN-based tabular generators, CTGAN and TABGAN, on subsets of the IDS data and compares their outputs using distribution and data-reduction similarity metrics as well as downstream ML classifier F1 scores, ultimately favoring TABGAN. CTGAN is run as one of two candidate generators evaluated in this comparative pipeline, using its conditional generator/discriminator design to model the tabular attack data.
paper-generation-alleviate-privacy-conce.needs: Full text not obtained; unclear whether CT-GAN was run via the sdv-dev package or a custom reimplementation, and the relative weight of CT-GAN versus TABGAN in the reported results.

paper-heart-attack-ctgan-2023.summary: Works on heart attack prediction, where accuracy matters more than usual and the available clinical records are few. A CTGAN model is developed for the prediction dataset, so SDV's conditional generator supplies the expanded training set.

paper-application-generative-adversarial.summary: This conference paper proposes a framework that generates synthetic tabular data for thermal processing performance prediction, using a 'train on synthetic data, test on real data' scheme feeding into a federated learning model to protect enterprise data privacy while mitigating data heterogeneity. The authors expand small-class samples using CTGAN and tune hyperparameters following recommendations of the CTGAN library, evaluating the impact of synthetic sample size on downstream prediction accuracy. CTGAN, with its mode-specific normalization and conditional generator trained by sampling, is run as the sole synthetic data generator underpinning the entire empirical pipeline.
paper-application-generative-adversarial.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package was actually run or whether the authors built their own 'table generation adversarial network' inspired by CTGAN's design. Integration marked unclear pending full-text verification.

paper-generating-privacy-preserving-synt.summary: This paper proposes a differentially private W-GAN-based method for generating high-quality, high-dimensional synthetic medical imaging data (e.g., radiology images) while providing formal DP guarantees, using selective noise addition to the generator to balance privacy and utility. CTGAN is mentioned only in a related-work list of prior approaches that attempted medical data generation without adequate privacy guarantees, and is not run, adapted, or otherwise engaged with in the paper's own method.
paper-generating-privacy-preserving-synt.needs: No full text available; CTGAN citation context is a brief related-work list, so deeper engagement cannot be confirmed.

paper-predicting-likelihood-airspace-use.summary: This article, published in Transportation Research Part C, develops a predictive model to estimate the likelihood that airspace users will reroute flights to mitigate air traffic flow management delays. Only metadata is available, so the paper's method and empirical setup cannot be confirmed beyond its stated topic. It cites the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper, but the manner of use (baseline, data augmentation, or passing citation) cannot be determined from this evidence.
paper-predicting-likelihood-airspace-use.needs: Full text and abstract not obtained; cannot verify whether CTGAN was run, used for baseline comparison, or merely cited in passing.

paper-comprehensive-review-medical-diagn.summary: A survey covering machine learning methods applied to medical diagnosis across studies published 2015 to mid-2020, summarizing algorithm types and disease areas and proposing future research directions. It is a review of prior literature rather than an empirical study of its own. CTGAN and TGAN are named only in a single passing sentence noting that deep learning methods can also synthesize tabular data, with no experimental use.

paper-timing-prediction-framework-wide-2.summary: This ASPDAC 2021 paper proposes a LightGBM-based framework to predict circuit path delays across wide-voltage PVT corners, addressing the scarcity of low-voltage timing data by augmenting training sets with synthetic samples. The authors reimplement CTGAN's conditional generator and discriminator architecture themselves, explicitly replacing the original ReLU activation with GeLU, and combine its output with SMOTER-generated samples to train the delay predictor. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional generator design are reproduced and modified in the authors' own implementation to generate the synthetic circuit-delay data underlying the whole empirical evaluation.
paper-timing-prediction-framework-wide-2.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package or an independent reimplementation was used, though citation to the CTGAN NeurIPS paper and description matches library usage.

paper-alleviating-class-imbalance-actuar.summary: This paper is a survey and applied study of Generative Adversarial Networks for actuarial data problems, covering GAN theory (explicit vs implicit generative models, VAEs, Boltzmann machines, WGAN) and then applying GANs to alleviate class imbalance and data scarcity in actuarial predictive modeling tasks such as fraud and mortality risk. It benchmarks GAN-based oversampling against SMOTE and other techniques on actuarial and public benchmark datasets. CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) appears only in the reference list among other GAN literature, with no body passage describing its use or architecture.
paper-alleviating-class-imbalance-actuar.needs: No body passage engages with CTGAN specifically; the paper's GAN discussion is generic (Goodfellow, VAEs, WGAN) so it is unclear whether CTGAN informed the authors' actual experimental GAN architecture.

paper-evaluating-drug-risk-gan-2021.summary: This paper proposes a drug-risk classification model for China's post-marketing drug regulation, combining feature selection, a GAN for feature-space augmentation, and SMOTE for sample-space balancing, then classifying with a random forest on CFDA spontaneous adverse-drug-reaction reports. The model is evaluated on hundreds of thousands of ADR reports and achieves high accuracy in distinguishing prescription and OTC drug risk categories. CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) appears only in the reference list among other GAN-related citations, with no evidence it was implemented or run.
paper-evaluating-drug-risk-gan-2021.needs: Full body text does not show any engagement with CTGAN beyond the reference list; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was discussed elsewhere in the paper's related work.

paper-synthesizing-credit-card-transacti.summary: This paper describes a system for generating realistic synthetic credit card transaction data, including both normal and fraudulent transactions, by modeling individual consumers and populations and simulating a virtual world of commercial life, implemented in a 40,000-line custom code base. The synthetic data is intended to support fraud-detection model training and hardware acceleration research where real financial data is scarce or privacy-restricted. The Synthetic Data Vault (Patki et al. 2016) is cited only as one of several prior proposals for generating synthetic data, without being used in the described system.

paper-tool-searching-sweet-spots-2020.summary: This petroleum-engineering paper builds a sweet-spot identification tool for shale oil horizontal wells, using gradient boosting classifiers (XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM) on well-logging features such as resistivity, porosity, and permeability. Because only a small number of horizontal wells were available for training, a Generative Adversarial Network approach is used to augment the training dataset before classification. CTGAN, cited from the SDV-family paper, appears to be the GAN architecture used to synthesize additional tabular well-logging samples for data augmentation.
paper-tool-searching-sweet-spots-2020.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm whether SDV's CTGAN package was actually run or whether the authors built their own GAN and merely cited CTGAN as prior work. Integration marked unclear pending full-text verification.

paper-synthesizing-quality-open-assets-2.summary: The authors present HealthGAN, a Wasserstein-GAN-based synthetic data generation method used to reproduce two prior autism spectrum disorder studies from a private health data warehouse while preserving patient privacy. They extend HealthGAN with a novel categorical/ordinal encoding scheme and evaluate the resulting synthetic data for privacy, resemblance, utility, and efficiency. The encoding scheme is described as a 'novel variant' of the categorical encoding method from the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV), which SDV's reversible transform technique is adapted and extended rather than run directly.
paper-synthesizing-quality-open-assets-2.needs: Unclear whether SDV's actual code (rdt) was invoked or only its published encoding design was reimplemented as a 'novel variant'; leaning derivative_work given explicit modification language.

paper-plurel-relational-scaling-2026.summary: Synthesizes whole multi-table relational databases from scratch rather than imitating an existing one, modelling schemas as directed graphs, primary-foreign key connectivity as bipartite graphs and per-table feature distributions through conditional causal mechanisms, and uses the resulting unlimited supply of databases to show that relational foundation model pretraining loss follows power-law scaling in both the number of synthetic databases and total tokens, with the gains transferring zero-shot to real benchmarks. The Synthetic Data Vault is the named prior art the framework departs from: it is cited for the premise that relational databases are rarely public because they hold sensitive information, and again as the privacy-preserving relational generator that reproduces the structure and statistics of a given real database but cannot produce novel ones from scratch.

preprint-profilefoundry-synthetic-person.summary: This preprint presents PROFILEFOUNDRY, a deterministic generator and fixed reference release of 100,000 synthetic adult Person Objects with households, employers, relationships, events, and provenance, intended as a reusable source layer for building downstream LLM privacy, memory, and agent-state evaluations. It positions itself against other synthetic-data and record-linkage tools rather than building on them, presenting comparison tables of related systems. SDV is cited and described in a related-work comparison table as a learned single-table, multi-table, and sequential tabular synthesizer whose relationships and sequence keys are supplied through metadata, but it is not run in the work.

preprint-unmasking-algorithmic-bias-pred.summary: This paper presents a reproducible GAN-based simulation framework coupling a spatial GAN with a Noisy-OR patrol-detection model to quantify how racial bias propagates through predictive policing pipelines, using multi-year Baltimore and Chicago crime data alongside Census demographics. Beyond the core bias-audit simulation, the authors evaluate an algorithmic mitigation strategy in which a Conditional Tabular GAN rebalances training data by racial group, finding it shifts but does not eliminate detection disparities. CTGAN, explicitly run via the sdv library (version 1.9.0), is used to generate race-balanced synthetic incident records for this debiasing experiment.

paper-mixup-structure-preserving-theory-.summary: Works out what mixup does to the moments of a dataset, showing that the usual interpolation shrinks the covariance and biases the expectation, and derives a mixing-weight distribution whose synthetic samples preserve both, which turns a heuristic augmentation into one with a stated structural guarantee. CTGAN and TVAE are the deep generative baselines the theory is checked against empirically, run from the synthcity open-source implementations, and the bias tables show CTGAN substantially disturbing the covariance and expectation that the proposed scheme preserves.

preprint-decentralized-federated-learnin.summary: This paper proposes a decentralized federated learning framework for collaboratively training probabilistic generative classifiers across peer-to-peer nodes without a central server, sharing local statistics to iteratively converge to a competitive global model. It is evaluated across varying network topologies, sizes, and non-i.i.d. data distributions. The vine copula synthetic data generation paper (Sun, Cuesta-Infante & Veeramachaneni 2019) is cited only in passing as one example of how probabilistic generative models support synthetic data generation.

paper-tabstruct-benchmark-2025.summary: Argues that tabular generative models are judged by criteria imported from image and text modalities and proposes structural fidelity - the alignment of causal structure between real and synthetic tables - as a fourth evaluation dimension alongside density estimation, downstream utility and privacy, then benchmarks nine generators from eight method families over seven datasets and reports that no single generator is strong on all four. CTGAN and TVAE are the GAN and VAE entries in that panel, and the benchmark's downstream-utility dimension is the train-on-synthetic test-on-real protocol adopted from Xu et al., which the paper also names as one of the inherited criteria it argues is insufficient on its own.

preprint-rural-medical-centers-struggle-.summary: This preprint studies how rural/satellite hospitals within a healthcare network struggle to produce well-calibrated clinical prediction models due to limited local patient volumes, and tests synthetic data generation as a way to augment local training data for model recalibration. The authors run CTGAN, TVAE, and GaussianCopula 'implemented in the Synthetic Data Vault' to generate synthetic patient records, using conditional sampling from CTGAN trained on all-site data to augment small local hospital datasets, and compare these against oversampling strategies. SDV's CTGAN, TVAE, and GaussianCopula synthesizers are run directly as the generators underlying the data-augmentation experiments that form the paper's core simulation results.

preprint-synllm-comparative-analysis-lar.summary: This paper presents SynLLM, a modular framework that uses 20 open-source LLMs guided by structured prompts to generate synthetic medical tabular data, evaluating statistical fidelity, clinical consistency, and privacy preservation across three public medical datasets. It proposes four prompt types encoding schema and domain knowledge as an alternative to GAN- or VAE-based generation. CTGAN is cited only in passing in the related-work discussion as a GAN-based method prone to mode collapse and requiring large training data, not run or benchmarked in the experiments.

preprint-clavaddpm-multi-relational-synt.summary: This paper proposes ClavaDDPM, a diffusion-model-based approach for synthesizing multi-relational (multi-table) data that uses clustering labels as intermediaries to propagate learned latent variables across tables via foreign-key relationships, aiming to capture long-range dependencies that prior methods miss. It is evaluated against PrivLava and other multi-table baselines on datasets of varying size and complexity. SDV's HMA-based Gaussian-copula relational synthesizer is run as one of the primary multi-relational baselines, and CTGAN is run as a single-table backbone model within comparison pipelines (ST-CTGAN, D-CTGAN).

preprint-differentially-private-generati.summary: This paper formalizes the problem of generating differentially private synthetic data when the input data has missing values, proposing adaptive strategies (partial marginal observation, DP-aware imputation) that improve utility across four real-world datasets under varying missingness. It benchmarks DP synthetic-data generators including PrivBayes, AIM, DPCTGAN, DPautoGAN and Kamino under its adaptive schemes, and analyzes the privacy implications of missing mechanisms. In related work it discusses Patki et al.'s Synthetic Data Vault framework, noting it uses Gaussian copulas to model low-way marginals from incomplete data but lacks privacy guarantees, describing it in prose rather than running it experimentally.
preprint-differentially-private-generati.needs: The tgan-2018 citation appears only in the reference list (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) and is not discussed in the body text provided; DPCTGAN baseline is attributed to a separate Fang et al. paper, not to the SDV-family TGAN/CTGAN work.

preprint-machine-learning-synthetic-gene.summary: A broad systematic review surveying machine learning methods for synthetic data generation across computer vision, speech, NLP, healthcare, and business domains, covering neural network architectures, deep generative models, and privacy/fairness concerns. It catalogs many prior works and datasets rather than running experiments itself. SDV's original paper is cited only in a reference-list entry among hundreds of other works, with no engagement in the body text.
preprint-machine-learning-synthetic-gene.needs: Body text passage around the SDV citation was not captured in the excerpt; judgment relies on reference-list context only.

paper-tabmt-masked-transformers-2023.summary: Applies masked transformers to tabular generation, treating each cell as a token to be predicted from the unmasked remainder, with ordered embeddings for numerical fields and a dedicated category for missing values so that incomplete tables train without imputation. TVAE is one of the four generators it is measured against, selected as the strongest VAE-based tabular baseline, and the comparison covers downstream classification accuracy across a range of datasets alongside correlation-error and privacy analyses.

preprint-improving-mixed-imputation-meth.summary: A preprint proposing improvements to GAN-based imputation methods for datasets containing mixed (categorical and continuous) data types, addressing missing data problems. No full text or abstract detail was available to confirm exact methodology or experiments performed. The work cites TGAN, the 2018 predecessor to CTGAN, as related prior work on GAN-based tabular data generation.
preprint-improving-mixed-imputation-meth.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether TGAN was run as baseline or only cited in related work. Judgment based solely on metadata.

preprint-disentangled-locally-fair-repre.summary: This paper proposes a disentangled representation learning method for fair classification, splitting embeddings into a sensitive-attribute-correlated part and an uncorrelated part, and applying a local fairness loss (balancing K-nearest-neighbor sensitive attribute ratios) only to the uncorrelated representation. It is evaluated on real-world tasks such as income prediction and recidivism prediction. The paper adopts CTGAN's preprocessing scheme -- one-hot encoding discrete values and normalizing continuous columns via a distribution representation scaled to [0,1] -- in its own input pipeline, but does not run the CTGAN model or SDV library itself.

preprint-copula-synthetic-generation-mac.summary: This preprint investigates whether copula-based synthetic data augmentation can improve machine-learning emulators of downwelling longwave radiation, reporting reduced mean bias and mean absolute errors when training on augmented data. The authors build their own copula-based synthetic-data approach (drawing on vine-copula methodology) rather than an existing tool, situating it among prior copula, VAE and GAN approaches to synthetic data generation. SDV's original copula-based synthesizer (Patki et al., 2016) is cited repeatedly as prior work demonstrating copula-based synthetic data for privacy protection and overcoming licensing restrictions, but is not itself run.
preprint-copula-synthetic-generation-mac.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract and citing sentences available. Cannot confirm whether SDV's actual copula implementation was used or only cited as prior art alongside the authors' own vine-copula method.

preprint-holdout-fidelity-privacy-assess.summary: This paper introduces an empirical framework for jointly assessing the fidelity and privacy risk of mixed-type synthetic tabular data, using holdout-based marginal distance metrics for fidelity and distance-to-closest-record analysis for privacy. The framework is demonstrated across seven synthetic data solutions and four real-world mixed-type datasets, comparing AI-based generators to traditional statistical disclosure control techniques. Four of the seven generators tested are drawn from MIT's Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) library, which is run as one of several synthetic data solutions being benchmarked.
preprint-holdout-fidelity-privacy-assess.needs: Evidence does not name which specific SDV synthesizers (e.g., CTGAN, TVAE, GaussianCopula) were among the four; metadata attributes the citation to the CTGAN NeurIPS paper but body text cites the SDV library paper (Montanez et al., 2018) instead.

preprint-self-training-method-semi-2017.summary: This preprint proposes a self-training meta-learning method for semi-supervised GANs, building on the Improved GAN framework, that leverages a GAN's own generated data to improve classification performance without extra labelled data. The SDV paper (Patki et al., 2016) is cited only in passing as an example of prior work on using generated data for data augmentation and model training, with no SDV component implemented or evaluated.
